items.title: Surjectivity on the f-squared kernels splits the eta transform into a direct sum of submodules
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring A, a nonzerodivisor f, and a complex M^bullet of f-torsion free A-modules, and assumes that the kernel of d^i modulo f^2 surjects onto the kernel of d^i modulo f; it concludes that the canonical map (1, d^i) from (eta_f M)^i / f(eta_f M)^i to f^iM^i/f^{i+1}M^i oplus f^{i+1}M^{i+1}/f^{i+2}M^{i+1} identifies the source with a direct sum of submodules of the target (source lines 27806-27819). The proof constructs an explicit inverse. With the notation of the earlier remark it defines a map t^{-1} from Z^i to (eta_f M)^i / f(eta_f M)^i by sending the class of x in Z^i, where d^i(x) = f^2 y, to the class of f^i x (proof lines 27822-27825). The substantive step uses the hypothesis: the assumption of the lemma signifies exactly that the domain of this operation is all of Z^i, which is what makes t^{-1} defined everywhere and lets the proof verify, in a step the author states is omitted, that it is well defined (proof lines 27826-27828). The proof then computes t composed with t^{-1} equals the identity on Z^i (proof line 27829), so that t^{-1} defines a splitting of the short exact sequence of the earlier remark, and the resulting direct sum decomposition (eta_f M)^i / f(eta_f M)^i = Z^i oplus B^{i+1} is compatible with the map displayed in the lemma, which is the conclusion (proof lines 27829-27836). The non-routine content is the construction of the splitting map and the identification of the hypothesis with the surjectivity needed to define it everywhere.
